Maintenance Report — MNT-0078-012

Asset: WELL-0078 (SW-24 Well 078, T200, Southwest Block 24) Equipment: rod string Work started: 23 Aug 2024 08:00 · Finished: 11 Sep 2024 12:00 · Well stopped for this job: 460 hours Crew lead: Brian Coleman (U-304) · Crew: Megan Ward, Daniel Foster · Contractor: Sandstone Rod & Pump Triggered by: inspection INS-0078-0096 on 2024-08-22 Report written: 12 Sep 2024

What happened

Field staff reported that the pump jack was running but the wellhead was cold and the rod load had dropped. The thermal reading at inspection INS-0078-0096 showed the wellhead at 35.0 °C with the air at 34.8 °C, so the well was not producing. The operator shut the well in for the repair. A dynamometer card showed no load from the downhole pump, which points to a parted rod. Sandstone Rod & Pump's workover rig was busy on other wells, so the well waited about 17 days for it; the work itself took about 2 days.

Root cause

A coupling unscrewed after repeated rod buckling at the bottom of the stroke.

Safety and permits

  • Pre-job safety meeting held with the crew before work started (WS-01).
  • Energy isolated: prime mover stopped at the bottom of the stroke, brake set and chained, motor disconnect locked and tagged, wellhead wing valve closed and tagged, pressure bled off (WS-02).
  • Personal H2S monitors worn; highest reading 1 ppm, below the 10 ppm stop-work level (WS-03).

Work done

  1. Rigged up the company workover rig on the well.
  2. Pulled the rod string and located the break.
  3. Recovered the lower section with an overshot fishing tool.
  4. Replaced the damaged rods.
  5. Ran the rod string back in and spaced out the pump.

Summary of the fix: fished and replaced parted rod section.

Testing and return to service

Pump test showed normal fluid delivery and the rod load returned to normal. The well was returned to production.

Parts and cost

ItemUSD
Sucker rods7,494
Rod couplings1,874
Fishing tool rental3,122
Labour (company crew and contractor)9,265
Total21,755

Compliance check

WS-03MetMonitors bump-tested; highest 1 ppm
WS-07MetWritten 1 day after the work (limit 3 days)

Notes and recommendations

  • Consider corrosion inhibitor treatment for this well.
  • Keep the recovered rod for failure analysis.

maintenance.action: Replaced the flange gasket and bolts and remediated soil
maintenance.report_html:
Maintenance Report — MNT-0078-013

Asset: WELL-0078 (SW-24 Well 078, T200, Southwest Block 24) Equipment: flowline Work started: 27 Sep 2024 08:00 · Finished: 28 Sep 2024 03:00 · Well stopped for this job: 19 hours Crew lead: Daniel Foster (U-302) · Crew: Megan Ward, Brian Coleman · Contractor: Tumbleweed Flowline Co. Triggered by: inspection INS-0078-0101 on 2024-09-26 Report written: 29 Sep 2024

What happened

The weekly drone inspection INS-0078-0101 at 11:45 on 2024-09-26 found crude oil on the pad: about 11.3% of the pad area, estimated 5.3 bbl. The inspector noted: "Oil sheen around cellar." The field operator shut the well in, closed the flowline valve and placed earth berms and absorbent pads. The release was contained about 8.1 hours after the inspection. The crew traced the leak to the flanged flowline connection at the wellhead cellar.

Root cause

A failed gasket on the flange where the flowline leaves the wellhead.

Safety and permits

  • Pre-job safety meeting held with the crew before work started (WS-01).
  • Energy isolated: prime mover stopped at the bottom of the stroke, brake set and chained, motor disconnect locked and tagged, wellhead wing valve closed and tagged, pressure bled off (WS-02).
  • Personal H2S monitors worn; highest reading 2 ppm, below the 10 ppm stop-work level (WS-03).

Work done

  1. Cleaned free oil out of the cellar.
  2. Unbolted the flange and removed the failed gasket.
  3. Fitted a new gasket and new bolts, torqued to specification.
  4. Excavated the stained soil around the cellar.

Summary of the fix: replaced the flange gasket and bolts and remediated soil.

Testing and return to service

Pressure-tested the repaired section at 201 psi (1.25 × the flowline's maximum operating pressure of 161 psi) and held it for 4 hours with no pressure drop (WS-05). The well was returned to production.

Spill clean-up and waste

  • About 4.0 m³ of stained soil excavated, bagged and sent to an approved disposal site under waste manifest WM-0078-013 (WS-06).
  • 4 soil samples taken around the spill; the highest result after clean-up was 0.23% TPH, below the 1.0% target (SR-03).

Parts and cost

ItemUSD
Flange gasket and bolts858
Absorbents and berms1,717
Soil hauling and disposal3,148
Labour (company crew and contractor)2,852
Total8,575

Compliance check

ProtocolResultDetail

WS-02MetEnergy isolated and tagged
WS-03MetMonitors bump-tested; highest 2 ppm
WS-05MetTested at 1.25 × maximum operating pressure, held 4 hours
WS-06MetOily waste manifested to an approved site
WS-07MetWritten 1 day after the work (limit 3 days)

Notes and recommendations

  • Inspect the remaining joints on this flowline.
  • Record the leak location for the flowline maintenance program (RC-05).

maintenance.action: Replaced gearbox seals and topped up oil
maintenance.report_html:
Maintenance Report — MNT-0078-022

Asset: WELL-0078 (SW-24 Well 078, T200, Southwest Block 24) Equipment: pump jack Work started: 07 Feb 2026 08:00 · Finished: 25 Feb 2026 18:00 · Well stopped for this job: 442 hours Crew lead: Brian Coleman (U-304) · Crew: Megan Ward Triggered by: inspection INS-0078-0170 on 2026-02-05 Report written: 26 Feb 2026

What happened

Field staff reported that the operator found an oil puddle under the gearbox. The thermal reading at inspection INS-0078-0170 showed the wellhead at 11.3 °C with the air at 11.4 °C, so the well was not producing. The operator shut the well in for the repair. The input shaft seal was worn and the gearbox oil level was below the sight glass. The well stayed shut in for about 16 days longer than the repair itself because heavy rain made the lease road impassable for the service truck.

Root cause

A hardened output shaft seal after years of service.

Safety and permits

  • Pre-job safety meeting held with the crew before work started (WS-01).
  • Energy isolated: prime mover stopped at the bottom of the stroke, brake set and chained, motor disconnect locked and tagged, wellhead wing valve closed and tagged, pressure bled off (WS-02).
  • Personal H2S monitors worn; highest reading 1 ppm, below the 10 ppm stop-work level (WS-03).

Work done

  1. Drained the gearbox oil into a closed container.
  2. Replaced the input and output shaft seals.
  3. Cleaned the base and absorbed the spilled oil.
  4. Refilled with the specified gear oil to the correct level.

Summary of the fix: replaced gearbox seals and topped up oil.

Testing and return to service

Ran the unit for 1 hour and checked both shafts for leaks: none found. The well was returned to production.

Waste

  • Used gear oil and oily pads sent to an approved disposal site under waste manifest WM-0078-022 (WS-06).
